record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: Let G=(V,E) be a directed acyclic graph. Eliminating a vertex j removes j and adds every edge (i,k) with i a predecessor of j and k a successor of j; the cost of eliminating j is |P_j|·|S_j|. A complete vertex elimination sequence is a sequence of such eliminations that transforms G into the corresponding bipartite DAG representation of the Jacobian, and its cost is the sum of the individual elimination costs. Given G and an integer k≥0, determine whether there exists a complete vertex elimination sequence whose total cost is at most k.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a directed acyclic graph with a set of source (input) vertices and a set of sink (output) vertices. For an intermediate (non-source, non-sink) vertex $j\in V$, let $P_j=\{i\in V:(i,j)\in E\}$ denote its set of predecessors and $S_j=\{k\in V:(j,k)\in E\}$ its set of successors. The operation of eliminating vertex $j$ consists of (i) inserting, for every pair $(i,k)\in P_j\times S_j$, the edge $(i,k)$ into the graph (if $(i,k)$ already exists, no duplicate is added), and (ii) removing $j$ together with all edges incident to $j$. The cost of this elimination is defined to be $|P_j|\cdot|S_j|$.

A complete vertex elimination sequence is a sequence of vertex eliminations applied to intermediate vertices of $G$ (and of the intermediate graphs produced along the way) which, when carried out in order, eliminates every intermediate vertex, leaving a bipartite directed acyclic graph whose edges go only from sources to sinks. The cost of the sequence is the sum of the costs of its individual eliminations.

Decision problem: Given a directed acyclic graph $G$ (with specified sources and sinks) and a nonnegative integer $k$, decide whether there exists a complete vertex elimination sequence for $G$ whose total cost is at most $k$. Determine the computational complexity of this decision problem.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint ("Structural Optimal Jacobian Accumulation and Minimum Edge Count are NP-Complete Under Vertex Elimination", arXiv:2506.17521) establishes NP-completeness of the structural optimal Jacobian accumulation problem under vertex elimination, resolving the long-standing open complexity question. The paper also provides an O*(2^n)-time exact algorithm that is essentially tight under the exponential time hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Structural Optimal Jacobian Accumulation and Minimum Edge Count are NP-Complete Under Vertex Elimination
status_evidence.snippet: Both problems are NP-complete, resolving longstanding open questions; provides O*(2^n)-time exact algorithms essentially tight under ETH.
status_evidence.claim: The vertex-elimination Jacobian accumulation decision problem is NP-complete.
